headline: Most US hiring managers are raising pay offers for candidates with AI skills, according to a Robert Half survey reported by Fortune.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from the pool score 5: the underlying data came out on 1 Oct (Robert Half 2027 Salary Guide); Fortune adds an interview and context.
importance_line: Workers with in-demand AI skills may see higher pay offers, which matters first to job seekers and people weighing retraining, then to employers competing for talent, but the figures are a recruiting firm's own survey of intentions and say nothing about workers whose jobs AI may replace.
summary: Fortune reports, citing new data from the recruitment firm Robert Half, that 72% of managers are raising pay for candidates with relevant AI skills and 42% say AI expertise commands more than other technical skills, while 57% are offering higher-than-planned salaries to attract new hires. The figures come from Robert Half's own 2027 Salary Guide, released on 1 Oct, and show employers' plans, not pay agreed; Fortune sets them against McKinsey's estimate that AI and automation will cut demand for 36 million US jobs by 2035 while creating 41 million roles.
notes: Old data re-reported on 5 Oct (Robert Half release of 1 Oct 2026); Fortune's own interview and context are new. Hold back as stale unless the AI-skills framing is wanted. Fortune says 1.7% average rise across specialties, Robert Half says 1.9%: not used.
